- Re-read the official Servosity OpenAPI at https://api.servosity.com/docs/?format=openapi (2026-07-26). `/dr-backups/` documents a required count/results envelope and DRBackup requires company (URI string), agent_session (AgentSession object), shadowprotect_keys (array), device_name (string), product_type (enum string), and encryption_key (DRBackupEncryptionKeyShort object), plus read-only integer id. `/backup-jobs/{backup_id}/` exists, but its 200 response contains only an empty description and declares no schema.
- At the pinned ca22b43 worktree, the committed focused suites pass: ServosityReadOnlyToolsetTest + ServosityClientSanitizationTest + BackupReadToolsMcpTest = 77 tests / 286 assertions; Pint --test passes on the five inspected implementation/test files. A direct adversarial invocation of the committed shared validator prints `MALFORMED_ROW_ACCEPTED` for a row with id=501, company=42 and null agent_session/shadowprotect_keys/encryption_key.

1. NOT RESOLVED — DR row shape validation is at the correct shared seam, but it is incomplete enough that malformed evidence can still become verified truth.
- RESOLVED portions: `liveDrBackups()` calls `assertDrBackupRows()` before building IDs (`ServosityReadOnlyToolset.php:332-355`); non-object rows and the predecessor's exact `{id:501}` fragment downgrade the whole read to schema_drift/UNKNOWN; no row is silently filtered; a documented empty results list remains status=ok/count=0 and is explicitly named a verified zero. Those are the right architecture and the focused regressions pass.
- BLOCKING remaining path: `assertDrBackupRows()` (`:608-630`) allows `company` to be an integer although the producer requires a URI string, and checks only key presence — not documented type — for `agent_session`, `shadowprotect_keys`, and `encryption_key`. Therefore `{id:501, device_name:'DONE-HOST', product_type:'DR_SERVER', company:42, agent_session:null, shadowprotect_keys:null, encryption_key:null}` passes the shared validator. `liveDrBackups()` then inserts id 501 into the trusted ID set (`:352-355`) and `upstreamCheck()` returns `verified_live` (`:430-431`). This is still a reachable malformed-row -> verified_live path, contrary to CLAUDE.md's “degraded read must SCREAM” convention.
- The claimed “full documented shape” fixture is itself authored to the implementation rather than copied from the producer: `drRow()` (`ServosityReadOnlyToolsetTest.php:145-157`) uses a URL string/null for documented object `agent_session` and a string for documented object `encryption_key`. Its green tests therefore miss the wrong-type path — exactly the CLAUDE.md rule that a mock authored from code under test proves nothing. Enforce the documented top-level types (without inspecting/projecting credential values) and add wrong-type regressions for every required field.

2. NOT RESOLVED — the refuted “structurally unavailable” premise is gone and the real endpoint is called, but its replacement still guesses the vendor response shape.
- RESOLVED portions: `ServosityClient::getBackupJobs()` calls GET `backup-jobs/{backup_id}/` (`ServosityClient.php:232-245`); `jobRunHistory()` uses it through the cached live-fetch seam with a reported 25-account cap and two-failure breaker (`ServosityReadOnlyToolset.php:454-546`). Request failures are `unavailable`, unrecognised responses are `shape_unrecognized`, outcomes remain explicitly UNKNOWN, and grep finds no stale `available=false`, “not available through this integration”, or “structurally unavailable” assertion in ca22b43 code/tests.
- BLOCKING convention violation: the official 200 response declares no schema, but `jobRunHistory()` assumes count/results and emits `records_observed` or a “verified zero” `no_runs_on_record` from `count` (`:492-513`). The tests explicitly fabricate that “standard list envelope” (`ServosityReadOnlyToolsetTest.php:16-29, 122-126, 255-308`) rather than use a captured vendor payload; the spec proves the endpoint exists but does not prove those fields or their semantics. This conflicts with CLAUDE.md's mandatory “field names come from the vendor producer” and “fixtures copied from the vendor's real payload” rules. Until psa-bh1i4 captures a real authenticated response, defer record-count claims or treat every response shape as unproven/UNKNOWN; do not call an inferred `count=0` a verified zero.
- TECH DEBT: psa-bh1i4's durable description is stale after R3 — it still says this tool emits `job_run_history.available=false`, and it is not linked to the parent. Update/link it so the accepted outcome deferral survives handoff accurately.

No regression observed in the previously settled planes: Comet unknown outcomes, Servosity count-map/container drift handling, freshness separation, staff explicit-grant boundary, standalone/no-tenant architecture, and thin service placement remain intact. No migration, controller, portal-auth, timezone, file-driver, or write-surface change is introduced.

title: UX/A11Y review: psa-z30dv Comet+Servosity backup read verbs @ 06b91ec
description:
PERSPECTIVE: ux / a11y — READ THIS SCOPE NOTE FIRST.

The primary consumer of this change is an AGEN …[truncated for fixture]
notes:
UX/A11Y review of 06b91ec against DESIGN.md and the landed psa-47vxh UniFi vocabulary.

Scope: This diff adds no new rendered interaction, status indicator, or layout. The only human-facing change is the plain registry blurb adding “Servosity,” which is clear. The Flat Rule, Signal Gold Rule, typography, focus/keyboard, contrast, and reduced-motion rules are therefore not implicated. The material UX surface is the MCP catalog and payload consumed by an operator’s agent.

Findings:

[P1] Servosity presents device provisioning as freshness-qualified when it is not. `ServosityReadOnlyToolset.php:57,125-170` says per-device enabled/provisioned state is synced and tells the caller to check `data_as_of` and each row’s `synced_at`, but device rows expose neither `synced_at` nor `stale`; the envelope is computed only from Servosity license rows. The underlying asset flags are deployment writes, not the daily license sync. An agent can therefore read an arbitrarily old `provisioning_state: provisioned` beside `data_stale: false` and confidently call it current. Separate the freshness domains: give device state a real observation timestamp, or mark it structurally unverifiable (`data_as_of: null`, `data_stale: null`, `freshness_note`) and require the live DR section for corroboration. This violates DESIGN.md’s Creative North Star “The Operations Desk” / “One operator, full picture”: the decisive uncertainty must sit on the decision surface, not be implied elsewhere.

[P1] Missing/malformed Servosity live shapes collapse to clean all-clears. `liveCompanyState()` sets `status: ok` and `account_counts: []` when `account_counts` is absent/non-array (`scalarMap()`), while `liveDrBackups()` turns a missing/non-array `results` key into `status: ok`, `count: 0`, and “reports no DR backup accounts.” Those states are indistinguishable from verified zero coverage. Treat absent/malformed required keys as `unknown`/`unavailable` with relay-ready copy, as the implementation already does correctly for missing `issue_counts`. Add drift tests for both seams.

[P1] An unknown Comet job status is asserted as a failure instead of unknown. `devicePosture()` maps the default category to `job_state: last_backup_failed` and increments the failure summary, even though `last_backup_status` says `Unknown (code …)`. Avoiding false success is necessary but not sufficient: this payload can make the agent confidently report a failure that was never established. Add a `last_backup_unknown` state/count and explicit note directing console verification.

[P2] Freshness vocabulary diverges from psa-47vxh. UniFi uses the common envelope `data_as_of`, `data_stale`, `freshness_note`; both new toolsets emit `staleness_note` only in stale cases. Keep `freshness_note` in the same envelope position and meaning across vendors. Also consider renaming `servosity_get_backup_status` to `servosity_get_backup_posture`: “status” suggests last-run outcome, which the description correctly says this integration cannot provide. Comet’s two verb descriptions are otherwise clear and make the start-here/drill-down choice explicit.

Positive notes: Comet lookup failures and no-job results degrade loudly; synced Comet rows carry `synced_at` + `stale`; Servosity’s `job_run_history.available: false` is structurally prominent; errors are generally plain and relay-ready; all added verbs are read-only.

VERDICT: REVISE — unknown or unverified backup data can still be presented as current, empty, or failed
close_reason: UX/A11Y review completed; findings and REVISE verdict persisted in notes.

notes:
PRODUCT REVIEW — 06b91ec against 9b326d4

Product value and scope:
- This is high-value for a solo owner or small MSP team: backup posture belongs beside client/asset context, and the three focused read verbs avoid both legacy-PSA clutter and write-path scope creep.
- Comet generally delivers the useful decision in one payload: configured/registered state, latest backup outcome, last success/failure, live observation time, synced-data age, and loud unavailable/no-jobs states. Empty alerts are correctly framed as corroboration only.
- Servosity is right not to invent a job endpoint. The always-present job_run_history.available=false block is an honest UNKNOWN and is preferable to a plausible all-clear. Keeping write/trigger actions out of this change is correct.

Blocking findings:
1. Comet turns an unknown vendor outcome into a reported failure. CometReadOnlyToolset.php:427-433 maps the default/unknown category to job_state=last_backup_failed, and the summary then increments last_backup_failed. The same row says last_backup_status="Unknown (code …)", so the machine-readable posture contradicts the label. Conservative does not mean inaccurate: the acceptance contract explicitly permits UNKNOWN. Emit a distinct last_backup_unknown/job_data_unknown state and summary count (with an explanatory note), and assert it in the existing unrecognized-status regression instead of checking only “not succeeded.”
2. Servosity’s per-device configuration/provisioning posture has no truthful freshness contract. ServosityReadOnlyToolset.php:57 tells the caller to check each row’s synced_at, but the device query/rows at lines 132-149 return neither synced_at nor stale. The top-level data_as_of/data_stale at lines 156-170 is computed only from license rows, so a fresh license sync can make the payload look fresh while enabled/provisioned asset state is unaged local workflow data. This repeats the psa-47vxh contract mismatch: freshness for one signal must not bless another. Either project the live DR-account check into a self-describing per-asset upstream verification state with live_checked_at, or explicitly mark local-only provisioning freshness unknown; do not call it synced unless there is an actual observation stamp. Add service and MCP-boundary assertions for each device’s source/freshness.
3. Servosity shape drift can still degrade to a clean empty while status says ok. liveCompanyState defaults a missing/non-array account_counts to [] (lines 220-224), and liveDrBackups defaults a missing/non-array results key to [] then says Servosity reports no DR accounts (lines 266-297). That conflates “vendor proved zero” with “expected evidence was absent,” undermining the same absence-is-not-health rule the change otherwise handles well. Validate these required containers and return an explicit shape_drift/unavailable/UNKNOWN state; keep a valid, present empty results array as the legitimate “no DR accounts configured” case.

Simplest product-correct revision: preserve the current three-verb surface and read-only scope. Add truthful unknown states and per-signal freshness; do not add a dashboard, write actions, or a guessed Servosity jobs API.

VERDICT: REVISE — Comet mislabels unknown outcomes as failures and Servosity per-device posture lacks truthful freshness.

title: SECURITY/DATA-SAFETY review: psa-z30dv Comet+Servosity backup read verbs @ 06b91ec
description:
PERSPECTIVE: data-safety / security.

=== FOCUS ===
1. *** CLIENT-DATA BLAST RADIUS. *** These verbs …[truncated for fixture]
notes:
Security review of 9b326d4..06b91ec (data-safety / security lens).

Authorization and scope — PASS:
- The verbs are exposed only on /api/mcp/staff behind VerifyMcpStaffToken and the existing 120/min transport throttle; they are not published on the portal MCP surface.
- All three are explicit-grant-only, are not inherited by legacy full-surface tokens, and are withdrawn when their integration is unavailable.
- client_id is normalized at the MCP boundary and passed as resolved context; the toolset prefers that context over conflicting model input. Local asset/license/alert queries are client_id-scoped. Comet additionally drops server-wide job rows unless DeviceID matches a registered asset for the resolved client.
- Inputs are parameterized/bounded (positive client IDs, parameterized hostname match, days capped at 90). No mass assignment, SQL/command injection, Blade surface, webhook, or vendor write/trigger path was added.
- Servosity API/TOTP secrets use encrypted settings; servosity_backup_password has an encrypted model cast and is deliberately excluded. No real secret was committed.

Findings:

1. HIGH — malformed Servosity live responses degrade to confident clean empties instead of UNKNOWN.
   - ServosityReadOnlyToolset.php:220-235 sets live.status=ok, while scalarMap($company['account_counts'] ?? null) returns [] for a missing/non-array account_counts and silently drops non-scalar values. issue_counts only checks key existence, so null/malformed content is also accepted under status=ok.
   - ServosityReadOnlyToolset.php:266-300 treats a missing/non-array response.results as [], sets live_dr_backups.status=ok, and emits “Servosity reports no DR backup accounts”. ServosityClient returns [] for invalid JSON, so this is a reachable response-degradation path.
   - Impact: an upstream schema change, partial response, or invalid JSON can convert “cannot determine coverage/issues” into “no accounts/issues”, precisely the confident-wrong backup posture this bead is meant to eliminate.
   - Required: validate presence and container/type shape before projecting; mark the affected section schema_drift/unavailable with UNKNOWN copy on any missing/malformed key. Add missing/null/wrong-type fixtures for account_counts, issue_counts, and results.

2. MEDIUM — raw vendor exception details are returned to the agent and written to application logs.
   - ServosityReadOnlyToolset.php:196-205 and :250-259 logs $e->getMessage() and embeds the first 200 characters in the MCP payload. Guzzle exceptions commonly contain the configured base URL and may contain vendor response text; a custom Servosity URL/infrastructure detail therefore crosses the agent boundary. The underlying ServosityClient already logs the same raw detail, so the new tool duplicates it.
   - Required: return a generic error/status to MCP, and log only redacted/structured diagnostics (operation + safe status/code/correlation id), never the URL, token, response body, or client PII.

3. MEDIUM — untrusted vendor strings are not consistently fenced or type-validated.
   - scalarMap() passes string values and all keys in account_counts directly to the AI surface. sanitizeStructure() fences string values in issue_counts but preserves vendor-controlled keys verbatim. A malformed/compromised upstream response can therefore inject prompt-shaped text into the junior-tech context.
   - Required: account counts should accept only the six production-proven keys and numeric values (or fail as schema drift); sanitize/bound any remaining external keys as well as values.

4. MEDIUM — Servosity per-device “provisioned” state has no freshness or reconciliation despite copy claiming it does.
   - ServosityReadOnlyToolset.php:132-150 derives provisioned solely from the locally stored servosity_dr_backup_id. ServosityDeploymentService sets that ID once; there is no daily per-device sync stamp or upstream deletion/unlink reconciliation. DATA_SOURCE_NOTE tells the agent to check each row's synced_at, but device rows contain no synced_at.
   - Impact: an upstream-deleted or unlinked DR backup can continue to read provisioned locally. The live list may contradict it, but the tool does not reconcile or flag that contradiction.
   - Required: describe this as historical local provisioning state, then reconcile each device against live_dr_backups (upstream_missing / agent_unlinked / verified_live) or add a real freshness stamp.

5. MEDIUM — vendor request amplification is only transport-limited.
   - One comet_get_backup_posture call can issue 25 AdminGetJobsForUser requests. At the route's 120 calls/min ceiling, a looping/compromised agent can drive up to 3,000 Comet requests/min. Every Servosity call auto-paginates the account-wide company list and then calls dr-backups; there is no per-tool/vendor cooldown, cache, or circuit breaker.
   - Required: add a short-lived per-client result cache/dedup or vendor-specific limiter/circuit breaker; retain loud UNKNOWN behavior when limited.

6. LOW — payload/log minimization can be tightened.
   - Comet responses expose comet_group_id, comet_username on every device/history result, and failed usernames; failure logging also records the username. These vendor account identifiers are unnecessary to answer backup posture and expand credential/client-identifier exposure. Servosity likewise returns raw company/DR IDs that are not needed by a read-only junior-tech workflow.
   - Required: omit vendor scope/account identifiers unless a documented workflow needs them; prefer PSA asset IDs/hostnames and aggregate failure counts.

Verification:
- git diff --check 9b326d4..06b91ec: PASS.
- Exact-commit targeted suites: 47 tests passed, 165 assertions (CometReadOnlyToolsetTest, ServosityReadOnlyToolsetTest, BackupReadToolsMcpTest).
- Four adversarial regressions were run in an isolated temporary worktree and all failed against 06b91ec, confirming: missing account_counts reports status=ok; missing DR results reports status=ok; exception URL/secret-shaped detail is echoed; prompt-shaped account_count strings are returned raw. The temporary test/worktree was removed after verification.

VERDICT: REVISE — Servosity response drift can produce false-clean backup posture, with raw vendor details also crossing the agent boundary

title: ARCHITECTURE/CORRECTNESS review: psa-z30dv Comet+Servosity backup read verbs @ 06b91ec
description:
PERSPECTIVE: architecture / correctness.

=== FOCUS ===
1. *** VENDOR SHAPE — DO NOT ACCEPT CODE-AUT …[truncated for fixture]
notes:
ARCHITECTURE/CORRECTNESS REVIEW — psa-z30dv @ 06b91ec (base 9b326d4)

Artifact and gates:
- Verified commit 06b91ec710de4f88090ce55e759961086c500b83 and reviewed all 12 changed files.
- `git diff --check 9b326d4..06b91ec` is clean.
- Isolated-checkout verification: PHPUnit 50/50 tests passed (405 assertions) across CometReadOnlyToolsetTest, ServosityReadOnlyToolsetTest, BackupReadToolsMcpTest, and McpToolsListResilienceTest; Pint is clean for all 11 changed PHP files.

Architecture that is right:
- The feature follows CLAUDE.md's thin-controller convention: business logic lives in vendor service/toolset classes; no controller, migration, write verb, tenant layer, portal-auth surface, or file/session driver is changed.
- Staff MCP boundaries are preserved: the tools are explicit-grant-only, live publication is config/OFF=OFF gated, the registry remains ungated for pre-granting, and client scope is resolved from the PSA client row rather than a caller-supplied vendor group/company. Registration is complete across AppServiceProvider, McpToolRegistry, ChetDataSurfaceTools, and ChetDataSurfaceToolExecutor. McpToolsListResilienceTest still exercises the delivered tools/list path and documents a flat query-budget increase.
- The Comet cross-bug check against psa-enpew passes: this code uses SDK `JOB_CLASSIFICATION_BACKUP = 4001` and the 5000/6000/7000 status ranges, filters posture to backup jobs, and does not copy the legacy CLASS_BACKUP=4 or exact-7002 behavior.
- Keeping Comet and Servosity as separate toolsets is the simpler maintainable design because their live APIs and honesty boundaries differ. A shared vendor-toolset base would be premature. A small shared freshness-envelope helper may be worthwhile, but is not required if both implementations exactly follow the canonical contract.

BLOCKING — Servosity's vendor/provenance conclusion is wrong and misses the parent acceptance outcome:
- The code/test comments say Servosity is closed-source and job-level run history is "structurally unavailable" because no existing production code consumes a jobs endpoint. CLAUDE.md explicitly forbids using existing consumer code as the producer and says a closed-source vendor's official OpenAPI is the next source. Servosity publishes that producer at `https://api.servosity.com/docs/?format=openapi`.
- That official spec documents GET `/backup-jobs/{backup_id}/`, `/backup-job-status/{backup_id}/{backup_date}/`, `/dr-backups/{id}/latest-success/`, and `/dr-backups/{id}/failures/`. Therefore lines 22-27/177-181 of ServosityReadOnlyToolset cannot claim structural unavailability merely because ServosityClient has no wrapper yet. The parent requires "did it last run / did it succeed." Obtain a captured authenticated payload (the two job endpoints' response bodies are not fully typed in the spec), prove any token/permission limitation, and then either implement the read or report the concrete upstream refusal as UNKNOWN.
- The test fixtures violate CLAUDE.md's hard-won fixture rule. `companyRow()` and the `drBackups` arrays are hand-authored to match the implementation; the Comet tests similarly instantiate and populate SDK objects rather than deserializing a vendor-produced fixture. "It is a real SDK object" does not make invented values a real response, and removed properties could become dynamic properties without failing this test. Derive fixtures from a captured response or vendor serialization/projection and cite the producer. The official schemas `CompanySummaryNg` and `DRBackup` already verify `issue_counts` and `agent_session_id`; the current comments incorrectly say no official producer was available.

BLOCKING — degraded Servosity shapes can still produce a confident empty/all-clear:
- `liveDrBackups()` treats a response with missing/malformed `results` as `status=ok`, `count=0`, then says Servosity reports no DR accounts. `ServosityClient::request()` also converts invalid JSON to `[]`, which reaches that false-clean branch. Validate the DRF envelope and make missing/malformed `results` UNAVAILABLE/UNKNOWN.
- `liveCompanyState()` turns missing/malformed `account_counts` into `[]` while keeping `status=ok`; only `issue_counts` gets drift detection. Apply the CLAUDE.md rule consistently to every field needed for the answer and add malformed/missing-envelope regressions.

BLOCKING — freshness does not mirror the canonical psa-47vxh idiom:
- Both toolsets use `timestamp < now()-48h` only, so a future-dated `backup_synced_at` or `licenses.synced_at` is classified fresh. The canonical UniFi implementation rejects future report times to UNKNOWN/stale. Add future-timestamp rejection and regression coverage.
- The canonical envelope always carries `data_as_of`, `data_stale`, and `freshness_note`; these toolsets substitute `data_source` and conditionally emit `staleness_note`, creating a second agent-facing idiom.
- Servosity device rows carry neither an observed/synced timestamp nor `stale`, despite DATA_SOURCE_NOTE saying each row has `synced_at`. `servosity_backup_enabled`/`servosity_dr_backup_id` are local provisioning state and have no freshness stamp. Either add a trustworthy observation timestamp or represent this plane as first-class UNVERIFIABLE (`data_as_of=null`, `data_stale=null`, actionable `freshness_note`) instead of implicitly covering it with license-sync freshness.
- Comet maps an unrecognized status code to structured `job_state=last_backup_failed` while labeling the status "Unknown." Preserve UNKNOWN as a machine-readable state; conservative must not become confidently false.

BLOCKING — Comet's slow-vendor path is unbounded:
- The vendor SDK's `Comet\Server` constructs a default Guzzle client with no connect/overall timeout, and CometClient does not replace it. `comet_get_backup_posture` can make up to 25 sequential live calls, so a slow server can hold the MCP request indefinitely rather than returning explicit unknown/unavailable. Configure bounded connect/request timeouts at the CometClient seam and retain the current loud per-username degradation. Add a timeout-path regression. Servosity has a 15-second per-request timeout; its unbounded `getCompanies()` pagination is remaining latency debt worth bounding separately.

Non-blocking merge debt:
- psa-enpew now has a fix commit for the legacy Comet constants. If that lands first, remove this PR's new CLAUDE.md wording that those services are still "under review" so living documentation does not become stale on merge.
- BackupReadToolsMcpTest proves a Comet tools/call round-trip but no successful Servosity tools/call round-trip or delivered Servosity freshness fields. Add that boundary coverage with the corrections above; direct toolset tests alone do not prove Chet receives the promised contract.

VERDICT: REVISE — Servosity job/provenance claims are incorrect, degraded shapes and freshness can fail open, and Comet live reads lack a timeout
